title: Understanding the Effect of Loss Functions on the Generalization of Recommendations

problem.claim: The effectiveness of loss functions for optimizing two-tower recommendation models is not adequately explained by Bayes-consistency analysis.

gap.claim: Softmax and OvA are both Bayes-consistent, yet their evaluation performance differs substantially, indicating a gap between theoretical loss properties and observed recommendation outcomes.

contributions.claim: Introduces ℋ-consistency for analyzing Top-k classification within the hypothesis space of two-tower models, with non-asymptotic and hypothesis-specific guarantees.
Shows that Softmax and Cosine Contrastive Loss exhibit ℋ-consistency, whereas OvA does not.
Relates loss-function theoretical properties to optimization behavior and practical outcomes in two-tower recommendation systems.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Theoretical analysis demonstrates ℋ-consistency for Softmax and Cosine Contrastive Loss but not for OvA.
The reported theoretical results explain the observed performance discrepancies between loss functions.
The findings are reported to bridge theoretical properties and practical outcomes in two-tower optimization.

narrative_sequence.summary: Two-tower models are prevalent in recommender systems because of computational efficiency and predictive capabilities.
The model separately encodes users and items and generates Top-k rankings from similarity scores, while optimization commonly uses Softmax or OvA surrogate losses.
Although Softmax and OvA are Bayes-consistent, their evaluation performance differs substantially, exposing limitations in Bayes-consistency as an analysis tool.
The authors introduce ℋ-consistency, establish differing consistency results for Softmax, Cosine Contrastive Loss, and OvA, and connect these results to recommendation outcomes.

source_observation.claim: Losses with the same broad theoretical property, such as Bayes-consistency, can still differ in recommendation performance.

interpretation.claim: Evaluation-aligned, hypothesis-specific analysis may reveal distinctions that general consistency notions miss.

application.claim: When comparing ranking losses, analyze guarantees relative to the model hypothesis space and target Top-k objective.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that ℋ-consistency alone predicts performance across other architectures, objectives, or datasets.

source_observation.claim: Softmax and Cosine Contrastive Loss are reported as ℋ-consistent, while OvA is not.

interpretation.claim: The choice of surrogate loss can affect generalization through its alignment with the ranking task and model class.

application.claim: Use task- and hypothesis-specific consistency analysis to guide loss-function selection in two-tower recommenders.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide empirical comparisons, dataset scope, or conditions sufficient to generalize the finding beyond the stated setting.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, and quantitative results are not specified.
The formal definition and proof details of ℋ-consistency are omitted.
Experimental conditions and implementation details are not provided.
